title: Minimum Wage Australia After Tax: Your 2026 Take-Home Pay Guide
description: See how the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour translates to annual, fortnightly and after-tax pay. Includes tax, Medicare and super for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: For the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours per week, your annual gross pay is $52,260, and after tax and Medicare your take-home pay is approximately $41,000.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Australia after tax for 2026?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026 the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. After deducting income tax and the Medicare levy (using the 2026–27 tax rates and 2025–26 Medicare thresholds), a single resident earning only this wage takes home roughly $41,000 per year. The exact amount depends on your circumstances, but this estimate assumes no other income, no HELP debt, and no salary packaging.

faqs.q: Does the minimum wage include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour is the base rate for permanent employees. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading, making the casual minimum rate $33.05 per hour. The loading is paid on top of the base rate and is intended to compensate for the lack of paid leave. When using our timesheet, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% to your base hourly rate – do not type a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on the minimum wage?
faqs.a: Superannuation Guarantee contributions are paid on top of your ordinary earnings. For 2026–27 the rate is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. On the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for 38 hours a week, your annual super contribution would be about $6,271 (12% of $52,260). This amount is not deducted from your pay; it is paid separately by your employer into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay from Hourly to Annual

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, converting it to an annual figure helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a 38-hour week, which is the full-time benchmark used by the [Fair Work Ombudsman](/topics/minimum-wage) and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the calculation accordingly.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is **$26.44 per hour**. For a 38-hour week that equals **$1,004.90 per week** and **$52,260 per year** before tax.

This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher than the national minimum. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement – the National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a target.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that makes the casual rate **$33.05 per hour**. The loading is intended to compensate for the lack of paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). When using our [timesheet](/), tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% to your base hourly rate. **Never type a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you.

## Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. For the minimum wage:

- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps you match pay cycles to bills and rent.

## Tax on Your Annual Pay

Australia uses a progressive tax system. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

In addition, the **Medicare levy** is generally 2% of your taxable income. The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles (2025–26) are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation.

### Example: Minimum Wage Take-Home Pay

For a single resident earning $52,260 (the minimum wage annual figure):

- Tax-free threshold: first $18,200 taxed at 0%
- Next $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) taxed at 15% = $4,020
- Remaining $7,260 ($45,001 to $52,260) taxed at 30% = $2,178
- Total income tax = $6,198
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,260) = $1,045.20
- Total deductions = $7,243.20
- **Estimated take-home pay = $52,260 – $7,243 = $45,017 per year**

This is an estimate. Your actual tax may differ if you have a HELP debt, earn investment income, or are eligible for offsets.

## Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of **12%** of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). This is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For the minimum wage:

- Annual super contribution = 12% × $52,260 = $6,271.20
- Your total employment cost to the employer = $52,260 + $6,271 = $58,531

Super is not included in your take-home pay; it goes into your super fund and is preserved until retirement.

## Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, weekly, and daily equivalents. Tick the casual loading checkbox if you are a casual employee. The tool uses the 38-hour week assumption unless you change it.

For more detailed comparisons, see our [reference tables](/data) which show gross and net pay for common hourly rates, including the National Minimum Wage and award rates.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
